## p132 A and C — An officer-register request and a garbled-message repeat

**Sources on this page:** p132 A, p132 C.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-p132-radio-service-p132-a-and-c--an-officer-register-request-and-a-garbled-message-repeat"></a>



**Source edition and verification: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

Childs p132 contains three separate records: a partly garbled request for
an officer-register extract, a conditional recovery of a repeat-transmission
instruction for Eilvese, and an exact request to repeat a garbled incoming
Caucasus message. The unchanged published `Nov4-6` key applies throughout.
The middle record has its own [canonical p132 case](#edition-cases-p132); A and C
have ordinary exact frames and remain separately catalogued physical sources.

The primary source is J. Rives Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX Cipher
System*, [printed p132, PDF page 135](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view).
The [full page](../../experiments/november_radio_service/sources/childs_p132_full.png)
is headed `5th NOVEMBER, 1918.`

<a id="edition-cases-radio-p132-radio-service-a-an-officer-register-request-with-the-name-unresolved"></a>

### A: an officer-register request, with the name unresolved

The [A source](../../experiments/november_radio_service/sources/childs_p132_A.png)
has this header and exactly 242 slots, including one printed dash:

<details>
<summary>Source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — clear header and/or literal source record:**

```text
A) OSM v OUI (9.29 p.m., November 5th)
HIER 13 2207
RICHI-242
```

</details>

The raw 121-position reading fixes 120 positions:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
MILLTAEGMISZIONKOSJOIIXUEBERTENDUNGEILESKRIEGSRANGLI?TRNAUSZUGESDESGENERALMAJRHYDEWALDERBETENXFELDEISENBAHNNHEFPAFR53540X
```

</details>

Six observed-coordinate substitutions and one dash fill repair ordinary
words, giving:

<details>
<summary>Exact edited proposal</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
MILITAERMISZIONKOSJOIIXUEBERSENDUNGEINESKRIEGSRANGLISTENAUSZUGESDESGENERALMAJRHYDEWALDERBETENXFELDEISENBAHNCHEFPAFR53540X
```

</details>

The readable clause is:

**Readable German — complete edited stream, with the literal addressee and name fields:**

> Militärmiszion `KOSJOII`. Übersendung eines Kriegsranglistenauszuges des `GENERALMAJRHYDEWALD`
> erbeten. Feldeisenbahnchef `PAFR53540`.

The readable quotation includes the entire opening `MILITAERMISZIONKOSJOII`. Its Z spelling and unresolved field remain literal; the six substitutions and one dash fill above are unchanged.

It requests an extract from a wartime officer register. **The addressee/place
field `KOSJOII` and the general-name field `GENERALMAJRHYDEWALD` remain
unresolved.** Neither is expanded into an identified person or place. The
raw `MISZION` spelling and `PAFR53540` footer also remain literal. This is a
partial source edition, not a securely identified personnel record.

A [separate surname proposal](../../experiments/p132_rohdewald_name/README.md)
reads `GENERALMAJ ROHDEWALD` at four additional observed-coordinate
substitutions, for ten substitutions and one dash fill in total. A 1913
*Deutscher Reichsanzeiger* personnel notice attests the surname Rohdewald
in a railway-general-staff context. This supports the proposed spelling;
it does not establish the officer's identity. The primary displays above
and the separate address proposal remain unchanged.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-p132-radio-service-b-repeat-the-fourth-period-telegram-in-the-fifth"></a>

### B: repeat the fourth-period telegram in the fifth

The complete source/model edition is consolidated in [canonical challenge
p132](#edition-cases-p132). That page combines Thomas’s initial fragment, Norbert’s
fuller sender-error reading and `VORHER` proposal, the later three-substitution
and two-erasure-fill account, and all four equivalent intermediate-`V`
positions. `p132_B` survives only as an identifier inside the frozen evidence
package; it is not a second catalogue entry.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-p132-radio-service-c-request-to-repeat-a-garbled-incoming-message"></a>

### C: request to repeat a garbled incoming message

The [C source](../../experiments/november_radio_service/sources/childs_p132_C.png)
has this header:

<details>
<summary>Source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — clear header and/or literal source record:**

```text
C) NKJ v LP (7.45 p.m., November 6th)
FUER COS 2150 (5/11)
RICHI-198
```

</details>

The 5 November origin line and 6 November reception line are retained.
All 198 coordinates and all 99 plaintext labels are fixed without repair:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
KAUKASUSDELEGAXWIEDERHLGVERSTUEMMELTEINGEGXOSKACHIX54GRXSSX1912XANXNACHCHEFERBETENXNACHCHE5X150527X
```

</details>

The message addresses the Caucasus delegation and asks for repetition of a
garbled incoming message to `NACHCHEF`. Its literal reference is
`OSKACHI 54GR SS 1912`; the footer is `NACHCHE5 150527`. Those abbreviations
and numerical labels, including the final `5` in `NACHCHE5`, remain as read.
No new numbering interpretation or silent spelling change is introduced.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-p132-radio-service-source-status-and-reproducibility"></a>

### Source status and reproducibility

The [inputs](../../experiments/november_radio_service/inputs.json) preserve
manual rows, literal headers, key provenance and source-image hashes. The
[certificate](../../experiments/november_radio_service/certificates.json)
records the raw and conditional readings, all possible label domains,
coordinate origins and exact forward witnesses. A remains partly garbled
at its names; B remains conditional on the extra-coordinate model; C is an
unchanged direct reading.

The period key is prior work by **George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and
Arno Wacker**, [2016, DOI 10.1080/01611194.2016.1169461](https://doi.org/10.1080/01611194.2016.1169461),
also reproduced in George Lasry's [2017-02-24 comment 4](https://scienceblogs.de/klausis-krypto-kolumne/2017/02/23/the-top-50-unsolved-encrypted-messages-46-unsolved-adfgvx-cryptograms-from-world-war-1/?all=1).
Earlier unreviewed OCR-derived candidates existed. The bounded paper check
found no explicit p132 body example; no universal first-decipherment claim
is made.

```sh
python experiments/november_radio_service/verify.py --verify
python experiments/november_radio_service/geometry_audit.py --verify
```

A [separate address-spelling supplement](../../experiments/p132_optional_address/README.md) prices `KOSJOII` → `KOSPOLI` at two additional observed-coordinate substitutions and binds independent raw occurrences in p90, p98 and p148. This optional proposal leaves the primary streams and unresolved name above unchanged.

## p132 — Repeat-transmission instructions for Eilvese

**Edition context:** p132 — Repeat-transmission instructions for Eilvese.

<a id="edition-cases-p132-p132--repeat-transmission-instructions-for-eilvese"></a>



Childs p132 B, received on 5 November 1918, instructs Eilvese to repeat a telegram and precede it with a signal. The conditional reading uses the published **Nov4–6** key and a model in which one extra `V` entered the intermediate coordinate stream.

<a id="edition-cases-p132-most-likely-reading"></a>

### Most likely reading

**Readable German — conditional extra-coordinate model, with three substitutions and two erasure fills:**

> Für Eilvese. Wiederholet Telegr[amm] von vierter Periode in fünfter.
> Gebet vorher 5 Min. VVV.

**Meaning:** For Eilvese: repeat the telegram from the fourth period during
the fifth. Send `VVV` for five minutes beforehand. The older imperatives
`WIEDERHOLET` and `GEBET` and the numerical `5` remain literal. `[amm]` only
expands the telegram abbreviation.

The [p134 repeat instruction](134.md#edition-cases-context-radio-instructions-p134-b--repeat-a-fourth-period-telegram-in-the-fifth) independently uses the fourth/fifth-period formula. The preceding `VORHER` signal clause is a p132 reconstruction, first proposed by Norbert in 2017.

<a id="edition-cases-p132-source-and-current-conditional-model"></a>

### Source and current conditional model

The [B source](../../experiments/november_radio_service/sources/childs_p132_B.png)
is marked with explicit urgency:

<details>
<summary>Source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — clear header and/or literal source record:**

```text
B) LP v NKJ (6.13 p.m., November 5th)
SSD EILT SOFORT LOESEN 1410 (5)
RIZI-155
```

</details>

The printed length and manual transcription both give **155 slots**. There
are two printed dashes in group `XFF--`; all other coordinates are retained.
The direct odd-frame reading has 77 paired positions and one unpaired coordinate:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — original odd frame; paired prefix and orphan coordinate reported separately:**

```text
FFEREILVESEXWIEDERHOLETT?LEGGWD3?MYMFLWF7MFFS7KFNT8RLTIWFWUAFQLL3F1QF7PZNMDQQ
```

</details>

The latter portion becomes readable in the opposite pairing phase. Under the extra-coordinate model, undoing the original transposition exposes four consecutive `V` coordinates at interim indices **54–57**. Removing any one gives the same 154-coordinate stream:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — conditional deletion of one V at interim indices 54–57 after untransposition:**

```text
FFEREILVESEXWIEDERHOLETT?LEGRXVO?VIERTERPERIODEINFU1NFTERXGEBETSORHER5MINXVVV
```

</details>

Three observed-coordinate substitutions and two printed-dash fills give:

<details>
<summary>Exact edited proposal</summary>

**Edited output — same conditional interim-deletion model, with the stated repairs and fills:**

```text
FUEREILVESEXWIEDERHOLETTELEGRXVONVIERTERPERIODEINFUENFTERXGEBETVORHER5MINXVVV
```

</details>

<a id="edition-cases-p132-exact-costs-and-the-four-equivalent-positions"></a>

#### Exact costs and the four equivalent positions

| Received source index, zero-based | Printed group / position, one-based | Change | Effect |
| ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| 52 | 11 / 3 | `X` → `F` | `SORHER` → `VORHER` |
| 64 | 13 / 5 | `A` → `D` | `FFER` → `FUER` |
| 88 | 18 / 4 | `A` → `F` | `FU1NFTER` → `FUENFTER` |
| 103 | 21 / 4 | printed dash → `F` | Missing `E` in `TELEGR` |
| 104 | 21 / 5 | printed dash → `X` | Missing `N` in `VON` |

The repair of `FU1NFTER` changes the affected coordinate within the word; the square's digit `1` and the numeral in `5MIN` retain their assignments.

Re-encryption of the 77-character proposal reintroduces the extra intermediate `V` before applying the original column order. All four positions produce the same 155-slot witness with **three observed substitutions, two dash fills and one extra intermediate coordinate**. Their differing source origins remain in the certificate.

The [geometry audit](../../experiments/november_radio_service/geometry_audit.json) compares all 156 one-insertion and 155 one-removal positions. For the stated wording, the four equivalent `V` removals form the unique minimum-cost set. Earlier insertion candidates and the full comparison remain in that audit; the result is conditional on the plaintext template.

<details>
<summary>Earlier readings and exact comparison</summary>

### Earlier source model and credited variants

<a id="edition-cases-p132-review"></a>

### Review

Norbert's marked extra `V` is intermediate 56; adjacent identical coordinates make its position within the run indistinguishable. His displayed rectangle also changes source 88 from A to X. That additional change produces `FUTNFTER`; the unaltered source reads `FU1NFTER`. The current wording instead uses the A→F repair in the table above.

`GEBET VORHER` is an explicitly published alternative to `GEBETSORDER`. Norbert compared the substitution pairs for `S` and `V`, noting the one-coordinate change. The present edition prefers this interpretation of the instruction while retaining both earlier proposals.

The [explicit editorial certificate](../../data/certificates/editorial_readings.json) maps the three readable normalizations to three additional coordinate changes, including the previously emended source position 88. Run `python3 -m adfgvx.editorial` to reproduce them.

<a id="edition-cases-p132-source-evidence-and-reproduction"></a>

### Source evidence and reproduction

The [current source inputs](../../experiments/november_radio_service/inputs.json),
[cipher certificate](../../experiments/november_radio_service/certificates.json)
and [geometry audit](../../experiments/november_radio_service/geometry_audit.json)
retain the native source, exact origins, all compared positions and forward witnesses. The package identifier `p132_B` is an evidence alias for this source. Source comparison and the current repair audit are by **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**; Thomas, Norbert and Max Baertl's earlier readings are reproduced above.

The period key is prior work by **George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and
Arno Wacker**, [2016, DOI 10.1080/01611194.2016.1169461](https://doi.org/10.1080/01611194.2016.1169461).
Their Eilvese discussion supplies the station context. The [source image](../../experiments/november_radio_service/sources/childs_p132_B.png)
is from J. Rives Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX Cipher System*,
printed p132, PDF page 135 in the [scanned volume](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view).

```sh
python experiments/november_radio_service/verify.py --verify
python experiments/november_radio_service/geometry_audit.py --verify
python -m adfgvx.editorial
```
